text: The bug is in the spiral loop: when the remaining sub-matrix is a single row (`top == bottom`), the "left along the bottom row" loop re-adds the same row in reverse; when it's a single column (`left == right`), the "up the first column" loop re-adds the same column. The fix is to guard those two loops.

gen_ai.operation.name: chat
text:
Now let me verify the fix by tracing the key cases:

- `[[1, 2, 3]]`: top row gives `[1, 2, 3]`; right column loop is empty; `top < bottom` is false so the bottom-row loop is skipped (previously it re-added `3, 2, 1`); left column loop is empty. → `[1, 2, 3]` ✓
- `3×4` matrix: outer ring gives `[1,2,3,4,8,12,11,10,9,5]`; inner single row `top==bottom` gives `[6,7]` with both guarded loops skipped. → 12 elements, each exactly once ✓
- `2×2`: `[1,2]` + right col `4` + bottom row `3` + empty left col → `[1,2,4,3]` ✓ (unchanged)
- `3×3`, `4×4`: guards are true for the outer ring, so behavior is unchanged → matches existing tests ✓
- Single column `[[1],[2],[3]]`: top row `1`, right column `2,3`, bottom-row loop empty (range is empty), left column skipped → `[1,2,3]` ✓
- `1×1` and empty/empty-row matrices: still fine ✓

The change is minimal: the bottom-row and left-column loops are now only executed when the remaining sub-matrix has more than one row / more than one column, preventing the double-counting that happened on single-row and single-column layers.

arguments.summary: Fixed the duplicate-element bug in `grid/spiral.py`: in the spiral loop, the "left along the bottom row" and "up the first column" passes were guarded with `if top < bottom:` and `if left < right:` respectively. Without the guards, when the remaining sub-matrix was a single row (e.g. `[[1,2,3]]`) or...
